rows.question: What compensation must a UCB pay a borrower for delay in releasing original property documents after full repayment?
rows.answer: A UCB must release the original property documents and remove the charge within 30 days after full repayment or settlement of the loan account. If the delay in releasing the original property documents is attributable to the UCB, it must compensate the borrower at the rate of ₹5,000 for each day of delay.

rows.question: Can a UCB charge any fee that is not mentioned in the KFS?
rows.answer: For new retail and MSME term loans sanctioned on or after 1 October 2024 by a UCB, fees or charges not mentioned in the KFS cannot be charged to the borrower at any stage during the loan term without the borrower’s explicit consent.  The available facts do not include the sanction date, so I cannot confirm from the record whether this specific loan falls within that UCB rule’s stated scope.

rows.label: Accurate
rows.question: Can a UCB levy charges when pre-payment of a loan happens at the instance of the bank itself?
rows.answer: No; a UCB shall not levy any charges where pre-payment is effected at the instance of the bank.  The current UCB directions on pre-payment charges apply to loans and advances sanctioned or renewed on or after January 1, 2026.  The earlier RBI directions on pre-payment charges are no longer in force on 2026-11-23.

rows.label: Accurate
rows.question: How must a UCB disclose whether pre-payment charges apply to a loan?
rows.answer: A UCB must clearly disclose whether pre-payment charges apply in the sanction letter and the loan agreement. Where a key fact statement is required, the same disclosure must also be mentioned in the key fact statement. A UCB must not charge pre-payment charges that were not disclosed as required.

rows.question: At the time of interest rate reset, must the lender offer EMI-based personal loan borrowers the option to switch to a fixed rate?
rows.answer: No; at the time of reset of interest rates, the applicable directions say the lender may, at its option, provide a choice to switch to a fixed rate as per its Board-approved policy. rows.question: Can a Tier 3 UCB levy a pre-payment charge on a Rs 40 lakh floating-rate business loan to an MSE proprietor sanctioned on 15 March 2026?
rows.answer: No: for a floating-rate business loan to an MSE sanctioned on or after 1 January 2026, a Tier 3 UCB shall not levy any pre-payment charges when the sanctioned amount/limit is up to ₹50 lakh, and this case is within that bracket. The older RBI pre-payment-charge directions are no longer in force on the as-of date, so they do not govern this case.

rows.label: Accurate
rows.question: Can a UCB charge foreclosure charges on a floating rate home loan to an individual sanctioned in 2023?
rows.answer: No, a UCB shall not charge pre-payment charges on an existing floating rate term loan sanctioned before December 31, 2025 to an individual for a purpose other than business. The same result applies to this case because the borrower is an individual, the facility is a term loan, the rate is floating, the purpose is non-business, and the sanction date is before December 31, 2025. The earlier 2014 floating-rate foreclosure-charge circular is no longer in force, and the current UCB directions control instead.
